newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Optimism grows in Staples merger.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Optimism grows in Staples merger.

text.p: Options activity Wednesday in Staples Inc suggested growing optimism among investors that its merger with Office Depot Inc will be approved, but maybe not until after the March expiration in about two weeks, traders said.
"It looks like there's a little enthusiasm the deal is probably going to go through, but after March," Frank McGarvey at TFM Investment Group in Philadelphia said.
The heaviest volume was in the Staples March 30 and April 30 puts, which traded 15,170 and 15,715 contracts, respectively, as investors rolled positions out one month.
Staples shares were up 2-1/4 at 24-3/8 in late trade, just off their 24-7/16 session peak, a 52-week high. Volume was heavy, at roughly 13.75 million shares.

"It looks like the arbitrageurs rolled out the puts to hedge their stock for the finalization of the deal," Michael Schwartz at Oppenheimer & Co said, referring to the heavy action in the Staples March and April 30 puts.
"That looks like the play," Schwartz said. "To protect against further delay of final approval, they're rolling out for an additional month's protection."

Last Friday, the U.S. Federal Trade Commission extended its March 5 deadline in the merger to give the two companies more time to negotiate with the FTC over the shape of the merger. A source said at the time the deadline was extended by "about a week."
The merger, announced last September, would create a company with more than 1,100 stores in the U.S. and annual revenues of more than $10 billion.
Other busy Staples options, which trade on the Philadelphia Stock Exchange, included the March 20 and 22-1/2 calls, which traded 5,460 and 5,000 contracts, respectively.
The March 15 and March 17-1/2 calls each traded more than 2,000 contracts.
In the April series, other busy options included the 20-strike call and put and the 22-1/2 call.
Trade was steady in the June and September series also.
Office Depot rose 1-1/2 to 22-3/8 on about 2.26 million shares.
Several Office Depot options were active at the American Stock Exchange, led by the March 20 call, which traded 2,640 contracts.
The March 17-1/2 put traded 2,050 contracts, the April 22-1/2 put traded 2,200 and the April 22-1/2 call traded nearly 1,700.
